status: Root-approved route: d01 to d10 designed and reviewed; d11 to d19 and i01 to i05 route-approved 1 Nov 2026, designs in progress. Owner rule 1 Nov 2026: new 2024 syllabus only.
identifierPolicy: Use the exact NESA CMS content-item codenames. NESA code fields are blank; do not label these as published outcome codes.
rootDecisions: Accept Codex brief 128 order and boundaries for d01 to d10.
d06 to d08 recall the Year 11 chain, product and quotient rules and extend them to Year 12 function families; they do not present the rules as new.
d09 uses applications L06 and d10 uses applications L09; applications L01 is kept for later exponential applications.
Site metadata labels (Year 11, Module 3/4) are never copied into video titles or descriptions.
Voice: Google AI Studio after the brief 124 pilot passes; no maths lesson is voiced before then.

Accept Codex brief 136 route inputs for d11 to d19 and i01 to i05 (1 Nov 2026). Production order follows the ids; playlist order may later place the trig-graph strand (t01 to t04) between d19 and i01 as the course outline recommends.
d11 to d13 recall d05 to d08 (sin/cos derivatives, chain, product, quotient rules) in one sentence each; they do not re-teach them.

d12 uses lesson 5 card 07 for the sec, cosec and cot quotient-rule derivations (site log item 50 was wrong; brief 142 corrects it) and adds original teaching for the graph-based cause, the domains and the co-function minus.
i01 owns many short definition points; the design groups them under one question (one curve chosen from a family by a condition) rather than listing them.
Integral videos i01 to i05 use the existing graph parts plus brief 136 kit needs; area-under-curve parts belong to i06 onwards.
laterHomes: Add later focused homes for tan proof, sec/cosec/cot, remaining trig composites and tangent/normal problems. These are mandatory actions omitted by the first-ten draft, not outgoing content.
After d10 teach physical modelling, continuity/differentiability, second derivatives/concavity and further graphing in a coherent route. The first ten are not complete calculus coverage.
